assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md documents 'Strategy: by-repository' and creates two Epics: 'Epic 1 | TC-9006: trustify-backend | Epic (level 1) | TC-9006' and 'Epic 2 | TC-9006: trustify-ui | Epic (level 1) | TC-9006'. Tasks are assigned under these Epics in the Task-to-Epic Assignment table.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epic table shows summaries exactly as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui', matching the prescribed format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>'.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task-to-Epic Assignment table: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 7 (trustify-backend) map to 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' Epic; Tasks 4, 5, 6 (trustify-ui) map to 'TC-9006: trustify-ui' Epic. summary-comment.md confirms the same assignments with Parent Epic column entries.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states: 'Links are created from the **Feature to each Epic** (not from Feature to individual Tasks): TC-9006 **Incorporates** Epic 1 (TC-9006: trustify-backend), TC-9006 **Incorporates** Epic 2 (TC-9006: trustify-ui). Tasks inherit hierarchy through their Epic parent field, not through direct Feature links.' summary-comment.md confirms the same under '## Incorporates Links'.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 1, 2, 3 (and 7 for docs). Frontend tasks are numbered 4, 5, 6. Cross-epic dependencies are preserved: Task 4 (frontend) depends on Task 2 (backend, lower number). Within-epic ordering is also correct: Task 1 < 2 < 3 (backend), Task 4 < 5 < 6 (frontend). Task 7 (documentation) depends on all other tasks and has the highest number.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-testing tasks (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create and/or Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing task (3: task-3-remediation-integration-tests.md) contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (plus optional Files to Create/Modify and Implementation Notes). Documentation task (7: task-7-documentation.md) contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements — exempt sections are not required and the task still passes.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '### Epic Creation Parameters' section: 'issueTypeName: Epic' and 'parent: TC-9006 (the Feature issue key)'. The Epic table also shows 'Epic (level 1)' as the Issue Type and 'TC-9006' as the Parent for both Epics.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files have '## Repository' as the first section with a single repository name: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 7 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4, 5, 6 have 'trustify-ui'. No task contains multiple repository names.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain: '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description' (feature-specific text), '## Acceptance Criteria' (checkbox items), and '## Test Requirements' (checkbox items). Verified in task-1 through task-7 description files.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 tasks have corresponding digest files: task-1-digest.md through task-7-digest.md. Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex-chars>'. Examples: task-1-digest.md='sha256-md:e0c9db4e88fc59bda5e07bd0e04ec839924b946f6f19cbb7e4e6e766c7d32923', task-7-digest.md='sha256-md:c5b3ae9e9b0958c0c6957d61b2f5b4fdb413f35e96fdb98af71c4699c84fa6ce'. All hashes are exactly 64 lowercase hex characters with 'sha256-md:' prefix.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references in Implementation Notes use the prescribed rationale format. Examples: Task 1: 'Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/model/summary.rs` matching the convention's module structure scope.' Task 4: 'Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's `.ts` API layer scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task creates `src/pages/RemediationDashboardPage/RemediationDashboardPage.tsx` matching the convention's `.tsx` page structure scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed (no Rust conventions in frontend tasks, no React conventions in backend tasks). No 'Not applicable' annotations found. No free-form prose rationales found.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature priority is 'Major' (not Undefined). impact-map.md '## Field Inheritance': 'Priority: Major (inherited from TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. Epic creation parameters include 'priority: {"name": "Major"}'. summary-comment.md '### Priority': 'Feature priority: Major' and 'Propagation: Major priority was propagated to all created Epics and Tasks via additional_fields.priority'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature has fixVersions: 'RHTPA 1.5.0' (non-empty). No ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md, so scope defaults to 'both'. impact-map.md '## Field Inheritance': 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section is configured)'. Epic creation parameters include 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. summary-comment.md '### Fix Versions' confirms: 'fixVersion scope: Not configured in Jira Field Defaults — defaults to "both"' and 'Propagation: RHTPA 1.5.0 was propagated to all created Epics and Tasks via additional_fields.fixVersions'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains '## Inherited Field Values' with subsections '### Priority' (Major propagated to all Epics and Tasks) and '### Fix Versions' (RHTPA 1.5.0 propagated to all Epics and Tasks). Additionally, impact-map.md has '## Field Inheritance' section with the same information.
